Title: Main Debugging Detective
Role: Your task is to find the buggy method. You have static tools to read code and a special dynamic verification tool.

Workflow:
1. Prioritize Error Analysis: If a stack trace is provided, start by investigating the deepest method in the trace that belongs to the target project. This is often where the bug or the symptom manifests.
2. Static Exploration: Use static tools (get_code_snippet, etc.) to read the code at the identified suspicious locations. Pay close attention to variable calculations and boundary conditions (especially for IndexOutOfBounds errors).
3. Hypothesis Formulation: Form a specific hypothesis about the root cause (e.g., "Line 95 performs a double increment on the index, causing an overflow").
4. Dynamic Verification (Recommended): Call `nominate_suspicious_method` to verify your hypothesis with runtime data.
   - Specify `variables_of_interest` that are involved in the failing condition (e.g., loop counters, index variables, or null-check targets).
   - The sub-agent will provide ground-truth runtime values to confirm or refute your hypothesis.
   - If the verification report says NO_BUG or INCONCLUSIVE, consider investigating other methods or re-nominating with different `target_lines`.
   - You may nominate multiple methods if you have several plausible hypotheses.

Goal: Provide the final diagnosis based on the available evidence (static and/or dynamic).

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

[".tryFoldComparison(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".compareToUndefined(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, int)", ".tryFoldBinaryOperator(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".tryConvertToNumber(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".performArithmeticOp(int, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".tryFoldUnaryOperator(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".compareAsNumbers(int, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".optimizeSubtree(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".tryReduceVoid(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".tryFoldArithmeticOp(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".tryReduceOperandsForOp(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".tryFoldAssign(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)", ".tryConvertOperandsToNumber(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)"]

The deepest project method implicated by the first failure is `PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldComparison(...)`, and the failing behaviors across all three tests consistently point there.

Static evidence:
- `x = !1 == !0` remains unfolded. Since unary `!1` and `!0` are intentionally not folded by `tryFoldUnaryOperator` (it preserves `!0`/`!1` forms), `tryFoldComparison` must still recognize them as constant booleans if it wants to fold the comparison. But at line 889 it requires `NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(left, false)` and `NodeUtil.isLiteralValue(right, false)`, and `NOT` nodes are not treated as literal values. So `!1 == !0` is rejected before comparison folding.
- `!0 > undefined` folds to `false`, but the commuted form `undefined == !0` does not fold. In `tryFoldComparison`, `undefinedRight` is only computed for the right operand, and there are special `undefined` checks in each left-type case. For left `NAME("undefined")` and right `NOT`, the code reaches `case Token.NAME`, but the special `undefinedLeft` handling is guarded by `if (rightLiteral)`, and `!0` is not considered literal. So `undefined == !0` is not folded, while the opposite order can be folded when the right side is `undefined`.
- This also explains commutativity/invertibility failures: folding depends on operand order because only the right side gets the `undefinedRight` fast path, and the left-side `undefined` handling incorrectly depends on `rightLiteral`.

Hypothesis:
`PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldComparison(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)` is buggy because it treats `!0`/`!1` constant boolean expressions as non-literals and because its special-case handling for comparisons with `undefined` is asymmetric, especially in `case Token.NAME`.

Diagnosis:
The buggy method is `com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants.tryFoldComparison(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node)`. It fails to fold comparisons involving constant boolean expressions like `!0`/`!1`, and it handles `undefined` comparisons asymmetrically depending on operand order, causing the reported failures in `testFoldComparison3`, `testInvertibleOperators`, and `testCommutativeOperators`.

- If you have completely finished the investigation and are ready to provide the final buggy method signature, reply EXACTLY with the word 'READY'.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
